title: Henderson moving away from stock to special arrangements; Don Redman
summary: Procope says Henderson was first to play manuscript arrangements, helped by Don Redman, and began arranging himself after Redman left.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: It was interesting what you told me, that he used to get arrangements of "Cavaleria Rusticana" and various classics for the band to play.
I don't think he recorded those.
No. No, he never recorded them, no.
No. But these were arrangements he wrote of the classics, or were they stock arrangements?
He was among the first, wasn't he, to get away from the stock? Wasn't that what really separated him in the beginning from other bands?
Yes, he was the first. I would say yes, that he was the first to play manuscripts, you know. Special arrangements, we used to call them. Because don't forget that he had Don Redman in the band.
He had Don Redman in the band and Don Redman was making all these beautiful arrangements. And I think during that time Fletcher was learning how to arrange.
Then after Don Redman left, then he started arranging for his own band, which is the way it should be, I think.
